items.prompt: A recipe is PATCHed with ingredients [{item: "Salt"}, {item: "   "}, {item: "Flour", qty: 2}]. Which positions do the stored rows get?
distractors: Salt 0 and Flour 2
Salt 1 and Flour 3
Salt 0, blank 1, Flour 2
items.explanation: The blank item trims to an empty string and hits continue before any insert, and pos++ only runs inside the insert, so Salt gets 0 and Flour 1.

items.prompt: POST /api/dishes arrives with { "name": "   " }. Which error message comes back with the 400?
items.answer: "name must contain valid text", from validatePayload in h()
distractors: "Name is required", from the dishes POST handler's own check
"Send a JSON object", since the body holds only whitespace
None: the name is trimmed to empty and the dish is created
items.explanation: h() calls validatePayload for every POST before the handler runs. A name that is blank after trim fails the name/title rule and throws InputError("name must contain valid text"), so the handler's "Name is required" line is never reached.

items.prompt: Why is the simple BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK tx(fn) helper safe in THIS app but not something to copy to an async PostgreSQL driver unchanged?
items.answer: It relies on a synchronous single connection; async drivers need a client per transaction
distractors: SQLite serializes every write anyway; the transaction is not really needed here
PostgreSQL drivers do not support issuing ROLLBACK from inside a try/catch block
The helper is re-entrant on SQLite but not on PostgreSQL, so nesting would break
items.explanation: fn cannot await, so no other request runs mid-transaction. The helper is also NOT re-entrant: a nested tx would issue a second BEGIN and SQLite would throw.

items.prompt: Dish and recipe deletes collect photo filenames inside the transaction and remove files after commit. What goes wrong with the cook-log delete, which removes files inside the transaction?
items.answer: A rollback leaves rows pointing at photo files that no longer exist
distractors: The files are never deleted, because fs.rm is skipped on rollback
SQLite locks the photo files, so fs.rm fails every time inside it
Nothing: fs.rm is asynchronous, so it always runs after the commit
items.explanation: A transaction cannot cover files on disk. Deleting after commit means a failure leaves an orphan FILE rather than a dangling ROW - the safer direction (review finding 1).

items.prompt: A cook log has empty changes, taste notes 'too salty', no process notes or next-time text, and two photos captioned 'top' and ''. What body does reindexCookLog store?
items.answer: 'too salty' then 'top' on two lines, with the empty values dropped
distractors: 'too salty' alone, as photo captions are kept out of the search body
Six lines, with blank lines kept where the empty values were found
'too salty top' on one line, with the parts joined by single spaces
items.explanation: The body is [changes, taste_notes, process_notes, next_time, ...captions].filter(Boolean).join('\n'): empty strings and nulls are filtered out, leaving 'too salty' and 'top' joined by a newline.

items.prompt: A user searches for: half-and-half cre. How does toFtsQuery shape that input for FTS5?
items.answer: Each term quoted, with a prefix * on the last term only
distractors: The raw text, passed through to MATCH unchanged
One quoted phrase covering the whole input
Split on hyphens too, with a prefix * on every term
items.explanation: It builds "half-and-half" "cre"*: double quotes are stripped, each whitespace-separated term is wrapped in quotes (so don't or half-and-half is not parsed as FTS syntax), and * is added to the last term for prefix matching. A query that still fails to parse returns [] rather than a 500.

items.prompt: An API caller creates a cook log with rating_taste: 9 and changes: 42. What is stored?
distractors: A 400, because validatePayload rejects out-of-range ratings
rating_taste 9 and changes "42"
Both stored as null
items.explanation: validatePayload covers dish and recipe fields only; cook-log fields pass through rating() (clamped to 1..5) and str() (non-strings become "") - normalised, never rejected: silent data loss for API callers (finding 3).

items.prompt: Why does isDate round-trip through toISOString() instead of only checking the YYYY-MM-DD pattern and Date.parse?
items.answer: So 2026-02-30 is rejected instead of rolling over
distractors: To convert the local calendar date to UTC before storing it
Because Date.parse returns NaN for every date before 1970
To strip the time component that Date.parse appends
items.explanation: cooked_on is a calendar label, not an instant; the stored string must equal its own ISO round-trip.

items.prompt: h() already validated that an id looked like a positive integer. Why was rewriting "01" to "1" a separate fix?
items.answer: Because validating a shape and normalising a value are separate steps
distractors: Because the regex /^\d+$/ already rejects ids with leading zeros
Because Express strips leading zeros only on GET requests
Because SQLite stores ids as text and "01" would create a duplicate row
items.explanation: h() validated that "01" looked like a positive integer but left it as raw text; a handler comparing text would disagree with SQLite's integer id. The fourth test asserts PATCH /api/dishes/0<id> returns 200 and the same id.

items.prompt: A client sends PATCH {"ingredients": [{"item": "Salt", "quantity": -1}]} (note: quantity, not qty). What happens?
items.answer: 200, because quantity is ignored and the one Salt row gets a NULL qty
distractors: 400, because the negative quantity is rejected just like qty would be
400, because validatePayload rejects unknown ingredient keys
200, but the existing ingredients are kept because the row is invalid
items.explanation: An allow-list validator checks only keys it knows and silently ignores misspelled fields - a good argument for rejecting unknown keys.

items.prompt: What does DELETE /api/logs/99999 return when no such cook log exists, and why?
items.answer: 204, because nothing checks that the cook log exists
distractors: 404, because h() looks the record up before calling the handler
400, because the id is larger than any existing cook-log id
500, because the DELETE statement affects zero rows
items.explanation: Each read handler checks existence itself; the delete handlers do not, so typos are invisible (review finding 5).

items.prompt: The log line says http://localhost:5274, and there is no authentication. Who can actually read and write the journal?
items.answer: Anyone on the network who can reach port 5274
distractors: Only processes on this machine, since the URL says localhost
Only browsers loaded from the Vite dev server's CORS origin
Nobody remotely, because Express refuses non-loopback connections
items.explanation: app.listen(PORT) passes no host, so Node binds every interface - the logged localhost URL is just text. Binding to 127.0.0.1 is the first change before running it anywhere but your own machine.

items.front: Why can the recipe page's 'best cook' and the dish page's best_score disagree?
items.back: Best cook picks the single log with the highest cookScore (mean of taste and texture, effort excluded; ties go to the most recent via strict >). The dish best_score averages taste over all logs and texture over all logs, then means those two averages - a different aggregate.

items.front: source_url is stored unchecked and rendered as <a href> (RecipePage.tsx:120-121). What is the risk and fix?
items.back: A javascript: URL is clickable - React 18 only logs a warning. Validate the scheme (http/https only) at the request boundary, and render untrusted URLs defensively; high severity once the app is multi-user.

items.front: Cmd+Enter in the cook-log editor bypasses the disabled Save button, and save() (CookLogEditor.tsx:56) has no guard. Why would adding if (saving) return; still not fully stop a double submit?
items.back: Two keydown events in the same tick both read the old state value before React re-renders. Use a ref (inFlight = useRef(false)) that is checked and set synchronously.
